name: AR-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Westerman with $4.7M cash on hand
model.rationale: Westerman is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by about 20 points, while James Russell has raised only a few thousand dollars. Prediction markets price a Republican win near certainty, and no polls or ratings suggest any competitive threat.
model.watch: A major outside-spending intervention or unexpected incumbent scandal could move the race, though nothing currently signals either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This southern Arkansas seat is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, and Bruce Westerman is seeking another term as its incumbent. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, holding more than $4.6 million in cash after raising over $2.5 million. His Democratic opponent, James Russell, has raised under $6,000 and has under $1,000 on hand, leaving him with essentially no resources to run a competitive campaign.

No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race, but prediction markets give Westerman roughly a 97 percent chance of winning. The district's strong partisan lean and the lopsided fundraising gap make an upset highly unlikely, and the forecast treats this as a safe Republican seat with a wide expected margin.
